REGULAR MEETING AGENDA - REVISED
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
AND SPECIAL MEETING OF THE CERRITOS PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY
MAYOR SOLANKI WILL PARTICIPATE VIA TELECONFERENCE FROM HIS ROOM AT THE
PULLMAN DANANG BEACH RESORT, 101 VO NGUYEN GIAP STREET, KHUE MY WARD, NGU HANH SON DISTRICT, DA NANG, 5500, VIETNAM
AND THIS AGENDA WILL BE POSTED AT THAT LOCATION IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE CALIFORNIA GOVERNMENT CODE
THURSDAY - DECEMBER 12, 2024 - 07:00 P.M.
CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CA 90703
Agenda Materials
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at cerritos.gov and at the Office of the City Clerk, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 1st floor, Cerritos, CA, during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the legislative body after distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made by email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by phone at (562) 916-1248 during regular business hours.
Order of Agenda
The City Council, by majority of those members present, may reorder the business items listed on the agenda.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at cerritos.gov, on cable television at Cerritos TV3, or in person in the Council Chamber.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting in person at the meeting or in writing as described below.
In-person public comment : Public comment on business agenda items will be opened and may be provided during consideration of that business agenda item. Public comment on Consent Calendar, Closed Session, and non-agenda items will be opened and may be provided during Agenda Item No. 6.
Written public comment (hard copy or email) : Public comment may be submitted via email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by hard copy to the Office the City Clerk at 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703 no later than 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 3:00 p.m. deadline will be distributed to the legislative body prior to the meeting and retained with the official meeting record.
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Office of the City Clerk at (562) 916-1248 or at city_clerk@cerritos.us in advance of the meeting to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the meeting.

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE SUCCESSOR
AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY AND SPECIAL MEETING OF THE
CERRITOS PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY HELD THURSDAY, DECEMBER 12, 2024, 7:00
PM, IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBER AT CERRITOS CITY HALL, 18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE,
CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA. MAYOR SOLANKI PARTICIPATED VIA TELECONFERENCE FROM HIS
ROOM AT THE PULLMAN DANANG BEACH RESORT, 101 VO NGUYEN GIAP STREET, KHUE MY
WARD, NGU HANH SON DISTRICT, DA NANG, 5500, VIETNAM, AND THIS AGENDA WAS
POSTED AT THAT LOCATION IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE CALIFORNIA GOVERNMENT CODE.

 1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

  At this juncture, Mayor Solanki requested Mayor Pro Tem Vo serve as the Chair of this
  meeting, as Mayor Solanki was participating in the meeting via teleconference.

 2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Pastor Jerry Maris, Calvary Cross Chapel.

 3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by the Cerritos Aquatics Club.

 4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency/Authority Member Bruce W. Barrows
  Council/Agency/Authority Member Lynda P. Johnson
  Council/Agency/Authority Member Frank Aurelio Yokoyama
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair/Vice Chair Chuong Vo
  Mayor/Chair/Chair Naresh Solanki

 5.  Presentations/Appointments

 5A.  Presentations

  A proclamation was made by the City Council honoring:

  Richard Martinez (Recognition of service as Parks and Recreation Commission Member).

  Tristan Chen, Jason Paul Gabertan-Tenazas, Nathan Shin-Lee, and Braedon Wan (Rank
  of Eagle Scout).

  Ishaan Khisti (10th Place – 1-meter springboard; 11th Place – platform diving, 2024
  USA Diving Junior National Championships).

  Xavier Zhang (10th Place – 3-meter springboard; 10th Place - platform diving, 2024 USA
  Diving Junior National Championships).

 5B.  Informational update on the Tuesday, March 4, 2024 General Municipal Election.

  An informational update on the Tuesday, March 4, 2024 General Municipal Election was
  given by Cynthia Nava, Acting City Clerk. A PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

  There was no further action on this item.

  The Mayor Pro Tem announced the meeting rules of decorum.

and Public Financing Authority Special Meeting

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  The Mayor Pro Tem opened the public comments period for items not listed on the
  meeting agenda but that were within the subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council,
  the Consent Calendar, and Closed Session.

  Cynthia Nava, Acting City Clerk, announced that prior to the meeting the Council/Agency
  members received full-text, unredacted copies of the one (1) written comment
  submitted for Item 6, by the deadline listed on the agenda and for inclusion in the
  official record. Requests for copies of the written comments submitted for this meeting
  can be made during regular business hours to the Office of the City Clerk.

  Seeing no further speakers, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  Announcement regarding Item 7B.2
  Cynthia Nava, Acting City Clerk, announced that the December 12, 2024 City
  Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting/Authority Special Meeting Agenda, listed the
  incorrect period ending date for the Council/Agency Treasurer’s Reports (Item 7B.2.);
  the correct period ending date would be captured on the December 12, 2024 City
  Council/Successor Agency/Authority Meeting minutes document (Item 7B.2.).

  Announcement regarding Items 7D and 7I
  Bill Ihrke, City Attorney, announced a summary of the recommendation for final action
  on the salary schedule and compensation paid in the form of fringe benefits, for any City
  employee defined as a “local agency executive,” pursuant to California Government Code

7B.3. Approval of Fiscal Year 2024-25 budget amendments (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Johnson, and seconded by Yokoyama, to authorize
  administrative initiated Fiscal Year 2024-25 budget amendments in accordance with
  Joint Budget Resolution No. 2024-12/CSA No. 2024-01 and the Strategic Financial Plan
  and Budget Preparation Policy (Policy 2.04) as adopted by the City Council, as follows:

  1. Account/Project: 110-631-61290 (Marketing Expense)
  Amount:  $200,000 (Transfer)
  Justification: A budget amendment is requested to transfer $200,000 from unused
  artist fees to advertising efforts for the Cerritos Center for the Performing Arts (CCPA).
  This transfer is necessary to provide an advertising boost for the remainder of the
  season, as the Season Brochure's effective shelf life has expired and additional shows
  have been added. The transfer will also partially restore advertising funding to previous
  fiscal year levels, supporting efforts to maximize revenues for the upcoming
  performances; and

  2. Account/Project: 110-552-97070 (Equipment & Machinery)
  Amount:  $203,000
  Justification: A budget amendment is requested for $203,000 in additional funding to
  support Phase II of the City's ALPR (Automated License Plate Recognition) camera
  program. This phase involves installing 22 cameras at selected intersections to enhance
  the City's burglary abatement strategy. Unlike Phase I, which required fewer cameras,
  Phase II includes wider intersections that demand specialized equipment to ensure
  comprehensive coverage (COUNCIL).
